 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellants-claimants, calling in question the judgment and award dated 21.08.2017, passed in M.V.C.No.551/2014, on the file of the Principal Civil Judge & CJM And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, at Ramanagaram (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) for seeking enhancement of the compensation.

Brief facts:
2. On 02.08.2014 at about 7.00 p.m., the claimant's father namely, Sri.Swamy was standing in front of Katakanapalya Gate.
At that time, the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-05-D-2286 came in a rash and negligent manner from Magadi side and dashed the deceased.
As a result, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the legal heirs under Section-166 of the M.V.
Act, claiming compensation for the death of the deceased in a road traffic accident.

sentences.text: The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.1,80,000/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondent nos.1 and 2 therein, jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellants-claimants and the learned counsel for respondent and perused the materials on record.
5.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:
1. Loss of Estate : Rs. 50,000/-
2. Loss of Love And Affection : Rs. 1,00,000/-
3. Funeral Expenses : Rs. 25,000/-
4. Transportation of Dead Body : Rs. 5,000/-
The Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards 'loss of dependency' on the ground that the claimants being son and daughter are majors.
Therefore, opined that they are not entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'.

This the approach of the Tribunal is not correct for the reason that even though both the claimants are majors, but they are unmarried and the daughter and son have crossed the age of majority i.e., just after 18 years.
Therefore, it cannot be said that they are not depending on the deceased.
Therefore, it cannot be said that they are not depending on the deceased.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' as per law.
7. It is stated that the deceased was a Mason by profession and earning a sum of Rs.600/- per day.
There is no proof of income for the work.
We also cannot expect any document proof for the type of work.

Therefore, as per Chart of notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, a sum of Rs.8,500/- per month is to be taken as notional monthly income of the deceased considering the accident occurred in the year 2014.

As per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd.
Vs. Pranay Sethi1

There are two dependants of deceased viz., son and daughter of the deceased.
Therefore, 1/3rd of the earnings would be deducted towards 'personal and living income'.
The appropriate multiplier applicable as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others.
Vs. Delhi Transport Corpn And Another2 is '13'.

Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss Of Dependency along with Loss of Future Prospects in Life' is Sri Honnaiah vs Sri Suresh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71290946/
3 recalculated and quantified as follows:
Rs.8,500 + 2,125 (25% of 8,500) x 2/3 x 13 x 12 = Rs. 11,05,000/-
8.
The Tribunal has committed error in awarding compensation 'Loss Of Consortium and Love And Affection' at Rs.1,00,000/-.

Therefore, as per the (2017) 16 SCC 680 AIR 2009 SC 3104 judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others3 and in the case of National Insurance Co.
Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi4, the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'Loss Of Consortium', along with 10% escalation.

9.
Further, a compensation of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded under the head 'Loss Of Estate' And 'Funeral And Transportation' respectively, along with 10% escalation.

Therefore, Rs.33,000/-
(Rs.15,000 x 2 + 10%) towards 'Loss Of Estate' And 'Funeral And Transportation'.
10.

11.
Therefore, the appellants-claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,26,000/- as against Rs.1,80,000/-.

The appellants - claimants are entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.10,46,000/- (Rs.12,26,000 - Rs.1,80,000) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of total compensation within Eight Weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.
